method.scope: Main content of the frozen thirteen editorial routes (Home, About, Projects index, seven original project cases, Experience, Photography, Writing index), plus genuine new /writing/* articles. CV, contact, legacy/redirect and 404 excluded.
method.word_rule: Unicode alphanumeric tokens; internal apostrophes/hyphens remain one token. Headings and alt text are not counted.
method.hidden_content: Unique content in hidden tabs/details is counted once; hidden state never removes real content from this audit.
method.exclusions: Navigation/footer/buttons/TOC/status/role/date/eyebrow labels, explicit UI instructions/placeholders and data-content-ignore/data-animation-copy regions.
method.deduplication: Across all measured pages in fixed route order: exact normalised paragraph/sentence duplicates removed. Sentences with at least 12 words also removed at >=90% token-sequence similarity, with comparable length and >=75% token-set overlap.
method.modules: Each nearest article/section/details container plus preceding content heading with at least one accepted body block. Titles themselves add no words. Structural heading changes alone do not prove a new editorial topic.
method.limitation: Same-word or near-copy inflation is suppressed; semantic information value and unsupported facts still require editorial review. The audit does not count photographs themselves as words.

Treating them as identical can produce a message that contains plenty of detail but gives the person encountering it no clear place to begin.

The issue is the distribution of information, rather than a decorative preference for fewer words.

The listener may not know the work being discussed, the reference a speaker assumes or the reason a particular image carries weight. In public expression, the language of delivery and the context of understanding are connected tasks, but they are not the same task.

The speaker could begin with the title and a plot summary, explain a convention of performance, or describe why one scene deserves attention. Each is a different invitation to the audience. Giving every possible piece of background would not necessarily make the introduction more useful; the details need a relationship to the argument being made.
